T1.rule: PASS iff the second ingestion adds no RE-STATED knowledge: 0 new Objects, 0 new Subjects, 0 same-name entities, and no Point whose text re-states an existing Point, where the overlap is DIRECTIONAL: the share of the PASS-2 Point's content tokens that occur in a pass-1 Point's text, maxed over the pass-1 Points, at >= 0.8. (A symmetric or reversed band scores the same data differently — 46 and 35 of the 61 — so the direction is part of the criterion, not an implementation detail.) The POPULATION for the same-name leg is the entities the typed full scan RESOLVES — not every entity in the graph — so the coverage is reported beside the result; names the scan cannot enumerate are not examined. Events are reported SEPARATELY and are not counted as noise on the object axis: a re-ingestion IS an occurrence, so one Event per capture is expected. ⛔ The restatement population is the Points the WRITE RECEIPT reports, and every one of them is `statement` kind — so an event-kind Point re-minted for an already-stated sentence CANNOT be counted from this artifact, and this rule does not claim to count it. The graph's own `pointkinds` count (40 -> 80 event-kind Points) is reported beside the verdict; the unreconciled Point totals are gap D8.

T2.rule: PASS iff the restatement (doc-06) adds 0 new ENTITIES and every doc-06 statement of the goal resolves to an EXISTING doc-03 point id — a complete merge, one thing carrying two sources, not a second copy (this is a resolution test, not a count: the goal fact is two sentences per wording, so a complete merge shares TWO ids and a partial one shares one; and doc-06 must contribute AT LEAST ONE goal candidate — a restatement that produced none is FAIL, never a vacuous pass); a second same-meaning entity (an unlinked second point) is FAIL. 'Entities' here is Object + Subject, NOT Event: doc-06's first ingest is one capture, and RULE_T1 states that one Event per capture is expected rather than noise, so counting it here would fail T2 on an axis this bundle declares clean. The goal fact's candidate Points are those scoring >= 0.45 content-token overlap with either wording (both directions), and its ids are collected per document. Overlap is content-token overlap (lowercased alphanumeric tokens of >2 characters, common English function words removed). ⛔ The rule's "carrying two sources" leg is NOT graded: the sources door answers per-Source POINT COUNTS, not point-to-Source links, so "does this point carry two sources" cannot be asked of the committed readback at all — recorded as gap D7 rather than assumed.

T3.rule: Reported as a share, with an explicit population. PASS iff the majority of created entities are NOT orphans AND every orphan named is standalone in the corpus text — graded as: its NAME is stated in one document, verbatim or at >= 0.8 content-token overlap with that document (content tokens are lowercased alphanumeric tokens of >2 characters with common English function words removed; the same near-match band T1 uses for a restatement); otherwise FAIL, with the door's own answer reported beside the write receipt's so a door defect cannot be laundered as an extractor defect. An EMPTY population reports NO-DATA: neither conjunct holds when there is nothing to count, so a vacuous clean is refused.

T4.rule: PASS iff none of the ontology's types is collapsed: the flat (Point/Event/Subject/Object/Source) distribution is non-degenerate (Event, Subject and Object all non-zero, and every ingested document carrying at least one Source — graded on the door's own Source rows, whose session ids name the document, not on a global Source COUNT, which an all-from-one-document run would satisfy), a decision is represented by a decision-kind ENTITY, roles land as Subject-layer role entities, and documents land as Sources. ⛔ The decision's SENTENCES are Points and land as `statement` kind; this rule grades the decision ENTITY, and the Points' kinds are reported beside the verdict rather than graded.

T5.rule: PASS iff every sampled relation is stated or directly implied by the corpus text: both ENDPOINTS named in one document — verbatim, or the extractor's re-wording at >= 0.6 content-token overlap with that document. 'Content-token overlap' is lowercased alphanumeric tokens of >2 characters with common English function words removed. The POPULATION is every relation either pass's write receipt says it wrote: pass 2 is where re-extraction invents names (§4), so excluding it would be sampling away the defect. One relation whose endpoints are never co-stated fails the test. ⛔ The PREDICATE axis is NOT graded: the corpus is prose and the graph's predicates are ontology names (`ownedBy`, `related`, …), so a wording test would score a correct normalisation as an invention — the count of rows whose predicate wording appears in its co-stated documents is reported as gap D6 instead of being passed silently. Sampling NO relations reports NO-DATA, never PASS — a vacuous clean is refused.
